b: Like our country, Vietnam is a Buddhist country too.. Wherever you go, the Buddha is there.. But nice people.. He hasn't grabbed every spot under the peepal trees.. So our Pillaiyar can go and sit there very comfortably, confident they won't seize his land ..But there the Buddha is a bit different.. They worship many kinds of Buddha, Lady Buddha, Avalokiteshvara, Laughing Buddha… And since there's a tall Lady Buddha in Da Nang, we set off to see her

Since these guys are crazy about the Nataraja service, they started walking.. And the sun started scorching me.. There was a leaf like a papaya leaf.. I plucked it and went along holding it over my head.. The rest walked without hats or umbrellas.. I'd stood in the sun like this before when I went to Trincomalee.. When I got home Amma was shocked at my colour.. I thought this would be the same story here

On the way they saw a path going up a hill and started climbing, saying this is the way.. It was a vertical staircase.. Terribly high too.. No people, no boards.. Here too, when climbing mountains, they find new routes like this and make it hard… On that belief I told them to climb and set off alone, saying I'd look for another path ahead

With Google's help I asked someone the way to the temple, and she showed me, it's ahead.. I'll do a separate chapter on this language problem.. I thanked her and found the place.. Then I phoned and got them down.. Otherwise these guys would have climbed all the way to the sky and caught the Buddha

There was a really enormous Lady Buddha.. Like our Avukana Buddha statue.. But she was dressed in layers and layers of cloth.. A fine white stone statue.. In the sun it dazzled the eyes.. But everyone looked at the Buddha as a decorative doll.. Used her only for photos.. In that sense our own Buddha is better off.. He's treated with proper respect.
After that we came back to the hotel.. They'd told us to check out at 12.. And we had to leave for another town..So we took everything and came out

That was the day I saw an Indian shop near the room.. I alone ran off before the car came to get a food parcel for myself.. Everything was terribly expensive.. In the end, to fit both hunger and budget, I took one paneer parotta, and he gave me a funny look as if to ask, will one be enough.. How could I tell him I'd come with mouth tied and belly tied.. Taking the food, we set off for the next town

The most beautiful thing in Da Nang is Son Tra beach.. Though it was close, we didn't go. The reason: everyone got up at nine.. after that, where.. That's why we didn't go. If you have friends who get up properly on time, take them and go and see it all.. The ones with me would say good night to the sun itself
With all this drama, the place we went to was Hoi An
note: "The Nataraja service" is Tamil slang for going on foot, after Nataraja, the dancing Shiva. The Avukana Buddha is an ancient standing statue in Sri Lanka. "With mouth tied and belly tied" means scrimping and saving.
